The Sacred Shrine

A Place of Divine Grace

درگاہ شریف رضویہ الہاشمیہ

The Dargah of Hazrat Syed Shah Ghulam Hussain Gulpir Razvi, located in Nasarpur, Sindh, is one of the most revered spiritual sanctuaries in the region. It stands as a beacon of Islamic heritage, Sufi tradition, and deep ancestral devotion that has endured for centuries.

Known as Gul Pir Jadar Razvi, the blessed saint was a distinguished Wali-Allah — a Friend of God — whose spiritual legacy traces back through an unbroken chain of Syed Razvi scholars and saints. The shrine is formally recognised as Dargah Sharif Razvia Hashimia, Nasarpur, Sindh.

The dargah continues to serve as a centre for spiritual gatherings, Quran recitation, and community prayer, drawing visitors from across Sindh and beyond. Its beautifully tiled exterior — adorned with blue and white Islamic tilework and golden finials — stands as an architectural testament to the devotion of generations.

✶   ✶   ✶
Sacred Wall Inscription

The Wall of Invocation

The entrance wall bears a magnificent tile inscription beginning with the Names of Allah, the Prophet ﴾﴿, and the Ahlul Bayt — a declaration of the shrine's Syed Razvi heritage and its custodians across generations.

Ancestral Heritage

The Noble Lineage

شجرہ طیبہ سجادہ نشینہ

سید میوں خدادّنو شاہ رضوی

Syed Mian Khadadnu Shah Razvi

Son of Syed Mian Imam Bakhsh Shah Razvi  ·  Successor No. 3

15 Jamad-ul-Awwal 1292 AH
1871 AD
14 Jamad-ul-Thani 1356 AH
1936 AD

The Shajra Tayyiba (Noble Family Tree) of this blessed shrine documents an unbroken chain of over 20 generations of Syed Razvi saints and custodians, formally certified on 8 December 1998 by Saeen Imam Bakhsh Adil Hussain Razvi, Wali-Ahd of the Dargah. The lineage traces through Dargah Hazrat Syed Shah Noor-Allah Shah Nouri Razvi and Dargah Hazrat Syed Shah Muhammad Hashim Shah Razvi.

✶   ✶   ✶
Sacred Artifacts

Ancestral Relics

تاریخی وراثت

Preserved within the dargah is a remarkable collection of centuries-old ancestral relics — ancient swords, ceremonial daggers with ornate silver handles, engraved brass bowls bearing Quranic inscriptions, handwoven Sindhi textiles, antique chinaware, and rosary chains — each a tangible thread connecting the present to a glorious spiritual past.

Sacred Archives

Manuscripts & Records

قدیم کتب و دستاویزات

The dargah holds a significant private library of ancient manuscripts, handwritten books, and genealogical records — many hundreds of years old — preserved under careful custodianship of the Razvi family.

These works include Shajra Namehs (family trees), Islamic theological texts, Sufi poetry, and historical documents that chronicle the spiritual and social history of the Syed Razvi lineage across Sindh.

The Community Today

موجودہ خاندان و مجلس
